title: Cross-segment streaming resume reconciliation and deterministic token accounting
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We have recurring customer reports and internal anomalies where resumed streaming sessions (client reconnects, network blips, or deliberate stream handoffs) cause duplicated or missing token attributions. The current pipeline assigns credits at fragment boundaries but does not deterministically reconcile across interrupted segments when fragments are replayed or partially resent. This leads to overbilling in some cases and quota denial in others.

Scope: Investigate end-to-end behavior from request ingress through tail-end billing aggregation and quota updates. Implement deterministic reconciliation logic so that: 1) every token is attributed exactly once across session resumes; 2) resumed streams re-use prior KV-prefix accounting state where applicable; 3) partial fragments and overlapping offsets are deduped without losing eventual consistency for downstream billing windows. Work includes protocol changes (resume token/sequence metadata), changes to the streaming metering aggregator, storage of lightweight per-session reconciliation metadata, and test harness updates for chaotic reconnect scenarios.

Out of scope: Long-term UX rate-limiting changes and quota policy design (handled by PM backlog), deep per-customer legal billing adjustments (handled by billing team).
acceptance_criteria: Reproducer harness that simulates reconnects, partial replays, and out-of-order fragments with assertions on final billed token counts
Deterministic algorithm implemented that marks fragments idempotently and reconciles overlapping ranges resulting in identical final token totals for a set of replay traces
No customer-facing billing deltas for steady-state non-resumed sessions (regression test), and corrected billing for previously failing reconnect cases in regression suite
Performance: aggregator CPU overhead + P50 latency increase < 5% for 99th percentile session loads in staging
E2E dashboard showing before/after reconciliation variance reduced to <0.1% for resumed-session workloads
Code review + security review completed and migration plan for state backfill documented
tasks: Design reconciliation metadata schema and resume token extension (owner: Tomas)
Prototype idempotent fragment id scheme and dedupe table (owner: Sanjay Rao)
Extend streaming ingress to attach resume metadata and monotonic offsets (owner: Maya Chen)
Update metering aggregator to consult per-session reconciliation state and apply deterministic merge (owner: Tomas)
Build chaos-driven test harness for reconnect/replay scenarios and integrate into CI (owner: QA Squad)
Load test in staging with production traces and verify performance (owner: Perf Eng)
Prepare migration plan for existing in-flight sessions and windowed backfill (owner: SRE)
Docs/Runbook for on-call: how to inspect reconciliation state and force re-reconcile for customer incidents (owner: Docs)
Submit PRs and drive reviews: streaming-proto, metering-service, billing-aggregator changes (owner: Tomas)
Coordinate with billing team to run small limited customer pilot (owner: PM)
comments: 2025-01-13 Tomas: Initial triage — reproduced issue locally by simulating a client reconnect after sending a partial fragment; observed double-counting when fragment id not durable across resume.
2025-01-17 Aisha: Decision to avoid heavy per-token state. Prefer a lightweight fragment-id + offset-range reconciliation table and eventual compaction. Tom to design schema.
2025-01-22 Sanjay: Prototype shows dedupe lookups are O(1) with a small in-memory bloom-check followed by persistent lookup for collisions. Memory overhead looks acceptable for P95 session counts.
2025-01-28 Maya: PR opened for resume metadata in streaming-proto: github.com/redwood-inference/streaming-proto/pull/412. Needs tests for cross-language clients.
2025-01-30 QA Squad: Added chaos tests that simulate 3 reconnects with overlapped 30% payload — current master fails assertions, branch passes locally.
2025-02-02 Perf Eng: Load test on staging with 10k concurrent sessions shows aggregator CPU +4% and tail latency increased by 3% at 99th percentile. Plan to optimize dedupe cache TTLs.
2025-02-04 Tomas: Merging staging PR after addressing compaction and TTL tuning. Next: small pilot with billing to validate on real traffic.
notes: This ticket aims to remove nondeterminism in billing for resumed streams. Implementation must be conservative: no retroactive customer charges outside pilot. Any backfill must be opt-in and coordinated with billing.
